properties.statement:
`reflow2_check.py` CRASHED ON A DIRECTORY ARTIFACT AND REPORTED THE CRASH AS 'GATE FAILED'. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`), 2026-08-15, and VERIFIED HERE IN EVERY PARTICULAR before being acted on.

WHAT THEY REPORTED: `IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: './.claude/'` out of `hash_file`, exiting 1.

VERIFIED, four ways: (1) `hash_file` opened the path with no directory guard; (2) `sys.exit(main())` had NO try/except, so an uncaught exception took Python's own exit 1; (3) the module docstring's contract is exactly as they quoted — '0 coherent · 1 gate failed · 2 could not run (… never a silent pass)'; (4) reflow2's own graph carries 182 artifacts with a location and NOT ONE resolves to a directory, against 11 in dev_storyflow.

⭐ THE EXIT CODE WAS THE WORSE HALF, and their framing is right: a dedicated code exists for could-not-run precisely so a CI job can tell a drifted design from a broken tool. Landing in 1 made the ONE confusion the three-code design was built to prevent reachable from every line of it. NOT a silent pass — that credit stands — but a MISFILED one, invisible in a badge or a required-check summary where the traceback is the only tell.

⭐⭐ AND IT IS THE SELF-HOST BLIND SPOT AGAIN, which is why reflow2 could never have found this alone: `ci.yml:102` runs this gate on every push and PR, against a graph with zero directory artifacts. THE GATE IS GENUINELY EXERCISED AND HAS NEVER EXECUTED THE BRANCH. The same shape as the kit-stamp finding earlier the same day — the maintainer's environment cannot produce the input that breaks the consumer's.

FIXED THE SAME DAY, both halves: a directory is now reported PRESENT AND UNHASHABLE, which the core already had a word for (`no_baseline` — 'cannot be judged, surfaced rather than treated as unchanged'), so it is a note rather than a crash or a quiet pass; and the entrypoint became `run_guarded()`, a NAMED function so the contract is callable and therefore checkable.

⚠️ AND THE FIX'S OWN FIRST TEST WAS WORTHLESS, recorded because it is the more useful lesson: it forced the fault with an unreadable export, which `die(2, …)` already handled, so IT PASSED WITH THE FIX REMOVED. Every fault this tool knows about is already routed to 2 correctly; the guard exists for the ones it does not. Caught by mutation-testing rather than by review, and only after a second error — the tests were first appended at the end of the file, which silently placed them in the NEXT test class, where they ran green in the wrong harness. TWO WAYS FOR A GREEN TEST TO PROVE NOTHING, both in one change.
